title: Affine denominator maps are injective on a full-support module without embedded primes
statement: Let A be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and M a finite A-module [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] whose support is Spec(A) and whose associated primes are all minimal primes of A. Let a and b be non-zero-divisors of A, let q be the localization of A at the multiplicative set of all non-zero-divisors (the total quotient ring), and put I = {x in A | x(a/b) belongs to A inside q}. Then I is an ideal of A (and hence is finitely generated), multiplication gives an injective A-linear map I M \to M, and the rule x m \mapsto (a/b)(x m), interpreted in the localization M_b and using that b is a non-zero-divisor on M, gives an injective A-linear map I M \to M. The cokernel of the first map is annihilated by I, and the cokernel of the second map is annihilated by the submodule (a/b)I of A.

source.place: Tag 02P2 (Lemma 31.25.5), affine proof after writing s=a/b

proof.text: The set I is closed under addition and under multiplication by arbitrary elements of A: if x(a/b) and y(a/b) lie in A, then (x+y)(a/b) lies in A, and for r in A one has (rx)(a/b)=r(x(a/b)). Thus I is an ideal. Since A is Noetherian, every ideal is finitely generated.

source.place: Tag 02P2 proof, definition of I and Noetherian finite generation

proof.text: A non-zero-divisor c of A lies in no minimal prime of A by [lem-pc-minimal-prime-avoids-nonzerodivisor]; since every associated prime of M is a minimal prime of A, c lies in no associated prime of M, so by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-module-zerodivisors-union-associated-primes] c is not a zerodivisor on M. Applied to c = a and c = b, a and b act injectively on M, and hence the canonical map M to M_b is injective. For x in I, the scalar (a/b)x belongs to A by definition of I, so multiplication by a/b sends IM into M inside M_b.

source.place: Tag 02P2 proof, paragraphs beginning 'For any A-module M consider the map 1' and 'Consider on the other hand the map sigma'

proof.text: Multiplication gives the first A-linear map IM to M. The preceding localization construction gives the second A-linear map by sending x m to (a/b)(x m); it is injective because a acts injectively on M (step 2) and M embeds in M_b.

source.place: Tag 02P2 proof, construction and injectivity of the maps 1 and s

proof.text: The cokernel of the first map is M/IM. Every element of I kills this quotient because i m is in IM for i in I and m in M, so it is annihilated by I.

source.place: Tag 02P2 proof, final sentence on M/IM

proof.text: The cokernel of the second map is M/s(IM). For i in I and m in M, the scalar (a/b)i belongs to A by the definition of I, and its product with the class of m is the class of s(i m), which is zero in this quotient. Hence the quotient is annihilated by the submodule (a/b)I of A.

source.place: Tag 02P2 proof, final sentence on M/s(IM)
